clue.text: Lacking adventure, indefinite number become participants in breaking revolt

indicators.note: the revolt is broken open so the other pieces can sit inside it

parts.note: an uprising is a revolt
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
to enter a contest is to become a participant in it

explanation.surface: A dull report on a rebellion in which an unknown number joined in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' splits the revolt word after its first letter to take the inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unenterprising shows no initiative or boldness, so lacks a spirit of adventure.

clue.text: Experience for Kaiser and therefore for Caesar

parts.note: und is German for and, as the Kaiser would say
ergo is Latin for therefore, as Caesar would say

explanation.surface: A sense of what both German emperor and Roman ruler went through.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it.

clue.text: Author of Eagles à la Campbell?

parts.note: ernes are sea eagles
Sir Menzies Campbell, a former Liberal Democrat leader, was nicknamed Ming, so in his manner is the Ming way

explanation.surface: Who wrote about eagles in the style of a Campbell?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as ERNES THE MING WAY: 'à la' means 'in the way of'. Ming Campbell led the UK's Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: B-blemish arising in state

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means going upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: the stutter in B-blemish asks for the word blemish stammered: a zit with its first letter doubled

explanation.surface: A stammering teenager is upset about a spot appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'B-' tells you to double the first letter of the blemish, ZIT, before turning it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tizz is a state of nervous agitation, a fluster.

clue.text: What police chief did perhaps is corrupt

definitions.meaning: a police chief might have ..., the detective branch, which split into two words is the answer

explanation.surface: A senior officer's conduct turns out to be crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food is rotten or putrid, the sense of corrupt as decayed.

clue.text: General hiding in grass did not move

indicators.note: one piece hides inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
main means general or chief, as in the main body

explanation.surface: An army officer stays still, concealed in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army rank but is the adjective, MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay put, staying where one is.

clue.text: Thread about weird club for particular group within society

indicators.note: the thread word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a suture is a surgical thread or stitch

indicators.note: a weird arrangement of the word club scrambles its letters

explanation.surface: Gossip about a strange club catering to a niche social set.
explanation.definitionFit: A subculture is a distinct group with its own values inside a larger culture.

clue.text: No award for the King's (as he'd put it) Miss Gwyn? That is … I won't have it!

parts.note: a Tony is an award for Broadway theatre

parts.words: the King's (as he'd put it) Miss Gwyn
parts.note: Charles II's mistress Nell Gwyn, whom the King would call our Nell
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Charles II refuses honours for his mistress, insisting he won't allow it.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was the actress mistress of King Charles II. The answer is British slang for 'certainly not!'
explanation.definitionFit: Not on your nellie is a British exclamation of flat refusal: no way.

clue.text: Track in the middle of wood is old

indicators.note: the single letter sits in the centre of the wood word

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: An ancient path runs through the heart of the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a narrow cut channel, like a track on a record.

clue.text: Inhabitant of cave beginning to investigate eastern religion

parts.note: a den is an animal's cave or lair

indicators.note: the beginning of the word investigate means its first letter only

parts.note: Zen is a Japanese school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A cave-dweller is studied as the first step into an Eastern faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is a resident or occupant of a particular place.

clue.text: Mafioso multiplying capital in seafood delicacy by twenty

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the seafood word is to be multiplied as a Roman numeral
fifty in Roman numerals times twenty gives a thousand, so that numeral replaces the first one

parts.note: lobster is a prized seafood

explanation.surface: A gangster grows rich in the shellfish trade, multiplying his money twentyfold.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L of LOBSTER is the Roman 50; multiplied by twenty it becomes 1000, the Roman M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a gangster, and a Mafioso is a member of the Mafia crime syndicate.

clue.text: Take a chance, moving knight over next to king

indicators.note: the knight's title is shifted round, read the other way
over in a down-style sense of turning backwards: the title is flipped

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player gambles by moving the knight over beside the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to gamble or venture, taking a chance on it.

clue.text: Inane insinuation voiced increasingly quietly

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out loud, so the sound of the phrase counts, not its spelling

parts.note: inane is dim and an insinuation is an innuendo, giving dim innuendo

explanation.surface: A silly suggestive remark is made, getting quieter and quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a diminuendo is a gradual decrease in loudness.

clue.text: This month staff blocking key payment

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters

indicators.note: the staff block the key, sitting inside it

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
men can mean staff, the workforce

explanation.surface: Employees fail to hand over a key payment this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is old commercial shorthand for 'of the current month'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one of a series of part payments of a debt.

clue.text: Prepared to be near the knuckle?

definitions.meaning: the knuckle is found on the hand, so something near it is literally on the hand

explanation.surface: Ready to tell risqué jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the knuckle' usually means rather rude; here it is read literally as a place on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Help that is on hand is available and ready for use.

clue.text: Portion including more than necessary (80%) sugar

indicators.note: the portion word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a dose is a measured portion

indicators.note: eighty percent of a five-letter word is its first four letters

parts.note: extra means more than is needed

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for a generous portion of sugar, more than necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: '80%' keeps four of the five letters of EXTRA, giving EXTR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is a form of glucose, a simple sugar.

clue.text: I'll write biography of academic, increasingly sick, losing heart

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic

indicators.note: losing the heart means one central letter goes

parts.note: iller means more ill

explanation.surface: An ailing professor plans to write a life story before he fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops one middle L of ILLER, leaving ILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiler writes a profile, a short biographical portrait of a person.

clue.text: 'Shut up!', heads of army training interjected — 'that's juvenile!'

indicators.note: interjected means thrown in among, so the picked letters go into the middle

parts.note: to immure is to shut someone up, wall them in

indicators.note: the heads of the words army and training are their first letters

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant yells 'Shut up!' during army training and is told he is being childish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like a shouted command, but it is the verb IMMURE, enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature behaviour is childish, like that of a youngster not yet grown up.

clue.text: Putin spaced out? Mostly resting uneasily

indicators.note: resting uneasily means tossing and turning, so the letters are mixed
mostly means the word resting loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The Russian president is in a daze, barely sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Putin with a space becomes 'Put in', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert something is to put it in.

clue.text: Dull broadcast rehearsal

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
a programme run is one shown or broadcast

explanation.surface: A boring practice transmission before the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a practice or trial before the real event.

clue.text: Uncle's an oddball, rejecting 50 Shades of Grey

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric, so the letters are rearranged strangely
rejecting means a piece is thrown out of the letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A strange uncle refuses to read Fifty Shades of Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: '50 Shades of Grey' looks like the novel; 50 is the L dropped from UNCLESAN before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle differences, the fine gradations between black and white.

clue.text: Llama regularly working to carry endless burden? Something like that

definitions.text: Llama regularly working to carry endless burden? Something like that

indicators.note: the rearranged letters carry, or hold, the other piece
working means the picked letters are put to work in a new order
regularly means taking every other letter of the word llama
endless means the burden word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pack is a load carried by an animal

explanation.surface: A llama is put to work hauling a load.
explanation.walkthrough: LAA, from 'regularly', rearranged by 'working' gives ALA, which holds PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpaca is a South American relative of the llama, used as a pack animal and for wool.

clue.text: Record collection of papers one after the other

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
a file is a folder of papers

explanation.surface: Archiving records and documents one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in single file means in a line, each behind another.

clue.text: Great United States!

parts.note: taken with States, this gives a second state, ME for Maine, joined to Georgia
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A patriotic cry in praise of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for very large or excellent.

clue.text: We hear you are in charge of waste

indicators.note: we hear means the words are heard, so their sound counts

parts.note: the letters U and R are said like the two words you are

explanation.surface: We are told that you run the waste department.
explanation.definitionFit: Uric means relating to urine, a bodily waste product.

clue.text: Read law wrong, getting unfair treatment

indicators.note: reading the law wrongly means its letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A law student misreads the statute and is treated unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is a harsh or unjust outcome for someone.

clue.text: Paint docked cycle getting blown up with air

indicators.note: blown up means exploded, so the letters are scattered and reassembled
a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of cycle goes

explanation.surface: A bike with its tail cut off has its tyres pumped up with air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' turns cycle into CYCL; that and AIR are mixed up by 'blown up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a quick-drying synthetic paint used by artists.

clue.text: Scatter cowry's shell randomly in wild shore? They might

definitions.text: Scatter cowry's shell randomly in wild shore? They might

indicators.note: scattering things randomly signals a mix-up of the letters

parts.note: the shell, or outside, of the word cowry is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Wading birds on a wild beach toss shells about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' mixes SCATTER, CY and SHORE together; the whole clue also describes the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Oystercatchers are black-and-white wading birds that feed along shorelines, picking at shellfish.
